To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) acquired resistance to sulfasalazine in human T cells is associated with upregulation of the ABC transporter ABCG2, and (b), this acquired resistance can be rapidly re-induced upon rechallenge with sulfasalazine.

(1) the ABCG2 efflux pump is a key factor in conferring resistance of human T cell lines to sulfasalazine; (2) this resistance is stable for at least several weeks after withdrawal of sulfasalazine and can be rapidly reinduced by rechallenge with sulfasalazine; and (3) the resistance is accompanied by a diminished responsiveness to the DMARD leflunomides and a markedly enhanced sensitivity to dexamethasome.
